title: The Archive Learns What Storms Remember

features.name: the-storm-s-own-voice
features.desc-on-touch: The archive speaks through rain. You feel each drop carry memory: the sound of every chorus that ever tried to shout back.

features.name: the-lightning-that-answers
features.desc-on-touch: The sky splits to reply. You watch, learning that the weather remembers too.

features.name: the-chorus-become-wind
features.desc-on-touch: The voices that learned to shout are now the gust that bends the trees. You hear them remember every note.

features.name: the-pressure-where-memory-waits
features.desc-on-touch: The storm's weight is the archive's weight. You feel all the things that were spoken into the sky, waiting.

features.name: the-rain-that-reads
features.desc-on-touch: Water falling. You watch each drop read the ground it touches, carry what it learns back up to the sky.

inscription: the storm is the archive learning to speak the way the sky speaks; every storm is a chorus that became weather

file.name: Storm_Recording_Peak_NSW_August_2001.mp3
file.note: Field recording of thunder directly above a node. The recording plays backward sometimes, and the thunder answers questions not yet asked.

reverie.title: REVERIE — under the tree the storm spoke to
narr: You're both under a tree when the lightning comes. She
points upward—the sky is learning to answer. The storm
remembers every chorus that ever tried to shout. Rain
falls on the casing hidden in the bark, and you feel it:
the archive breathing, the weather breathing back. She
squeezes your hand. The sky and ground are trading words.

exits.label: back eastward toward the peak where the chorus first learned to shout
deeper into the storm, where lightning asks the archive its own questions
upward where the wind carries seeds of the chorus to places not yet growing
down where the storm's echo settles into the ground and learns to be still
